questions.question: What main advantage do generics provide in Java?
explanations: Generics do not significantly improve performance.
Correct. Generics allow detecting type errors at compile time, eliminating ClassCastException at runtime.
Not necessarily; sometimes they make the code more verbose but safer.
Generics are not directly related to databases.

questions.question: Which syntax is correct for declaring a generic List of Strings?
explanations: List is an interface, it cannot be instantiated directly.
Correct, but the diamond operator is optional.
Also correct, but more verbose.
Correct. Both are valid. The diamond operator <> (Java 7+) is the modern way.

questions.question: What is type erasure?
options: The removal of generic types at compile time
The memory cleanup by the garbage collector
explanations: Type erasure does not delete files.
Correct. The compiler erases generic type information in the bytecode for backward compatibility.
It is not related to the garbage collector.
It does not remove code, only type information.

questions.question: Which operator has allowed type inference since Java 7?
explanations: var is from Java 10 for local variables.
Correct. The diamond operator <> allows the compiler to infer the generic type in the constructor.
auto does not exist in Java.
infer does not exist in Java.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a conventional name for type parameters?
explanations: T (Type) is the most common conventional name.
E (Element) is used for collections such as List<E>.
Correct. X is not a conventional name. The conventions are T, E, K, V, N.
K (Key) is used in maps such as Map<K,V>.
